LCL is charged per W/M, which means weight or measure: one tonne or one cubic metre, whichever is greater. Dense cargo is charged by weight and light, bulky cargo by volume. Most lines and consolidators also apply a minimum charge.
When does a full container become cheaper than LCL?

When your cargo fills enough of the box that the container price is lower than the W/M rate times your cargo. The calculator shows that break-even point in W/M and as a share of the container. It is often around half to two thirds of a 20 foot or 40 foot box, but it depends entirely on the two quotes.
Why is air freight counted at 167 kg per cubic metre?

Airlines charge on the higher of actual weight and volumetric weight. The IATA standard divides volume by 6000 cubic centimetres per kilogram, which equals 167 kg per cubic metre. Light, bulky cargo therefore costs much more by air than its weight suggests.
Why does the sea or air result include a cost of money?

Goods on a ship are stock you have paid for but cannot sell. The extra weeks at sea tie up that cash. Putting a yearly cost on it shows whether the saving on freight really beats the cost of waiting. Set it to zero to compare freight only.
